html:
Spanish Hispaniola was the first Spanish colony in the Americas, on the Caribbean island now shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic. Christopher Columbus founded the first settlement in 1493, and Santo Domingo became its capital.

For a generation it was the base of Spain in the New World. The island's Taíno were forced into labour under the encomienda system and died in huge numbers from overwork and disease. Spaniards built the first sugar mills there and brought enslaved Africans to work them.

Once Mexico and Peru were conquered, settlers left for richer lands, and the colony became a backwater. In 1605 and 1606 the governor emptied the north and west coasts to stop smuggling. French buccaneers moved into the empty west, and in 1697 Spain gave up the western third, which became Saint-Domingue and later Haiti. Spain ceded the rest to France in 1795, held it again from 1809, and lost it in 1821. The map continues it as Santo Domingo.
sum: Spanish Hispaniola was the first Spanish colony in the Americas, on the Caribbean island now shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic. Christopher Columbus founded the first settlement in 1493, and Santo Domingo became its capital.
